subject.title: [Bug]: ACP concurrent session spawns — first agent fails to launch CC process

question: Should OpenClaw preserve concurrent distinct ACP child-session launches and fix launch readiness, or intentionally serialize/gate ACP backend starts when using acpx/Claude?
rationale: Current main deliberately allows distinct ACP sessions to run in parallel, so changing that behavior would trade multi-agent throughput for startup safety and needs maintainer intent before an automated repair changes concurrency semantics.

options.title: Keep concurrency and fix readiness
options.body: Preserve distinct ACP child-session concurrency, add launch/readiness/error detection around backend startup, and prove both children emit output in a live ACPX/Claude run.

options.title: Serialize acpx child launches
options.body: Queue ACP backend starts per backend or agent so rapid spawns cannot race, accepting slower multi-agent startup as the compatibility tradeoff.

options.title: Document unsupported concurrency
options.body: Keep runtime behavior as-is and document that acpx/Claude concurrent child launches require caller-side spacing or separate direct execution.

recommendation.title: Keep concurrency and fix readiness
recommendation.body: Preserve distinct ACP child-session concurrency, add launch/readiness/error detection around backend startup, and prove both children emit output in a live ACPX/Claude run.

likelyOwner.reason: The central ACP spawn/control-plane behavior appears to originate in this person's ACP thread-bound agents work, making them the strongest routing candidate for the concurrency-policy question.
